mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% indicates an ultra-accommodative monetary policy, which compresses discount rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) and GDP growth below 1.5% annualized signals economic contraction, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100 and GDPC1 growth rate < 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Post-FOMC rate cut periods feature immediate market anticipation of accommodative policy, reducing equity discount rates and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are negative in > 60% of instances following FOMC rate cuts.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 1,050 thousand units reflect robust consumer demand and construction activity, supporting economic expansion and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1,050.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate above 4.5% indicates restrictive monetary policy, increasing borrowing costs and reducing economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent employment decline (PAYEMS change < 0) and unemployment rise (>0.1pp) signal labor market contraction, reducing consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise > 0.1pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises > 0.1pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, industrial production above 105 (index 2017=100) reflects robust manufacturing output, supporting corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are negative in > 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion when INDPRO > 105.
